title: Workflows or agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: Which statement correctly tells a workflow apart from an agent?

options.text: A workflow uses tools, while an agent never calls any tools
A workflow calls the model once, while an agent calls it often
A workflow's code fixes the steps, while an agent's model picks them
A workflow has no model inside it, while an agent always has one

items.stem: A makerspace booking feature always runs the same three steps in the same order. Step 1: the model reads the student's message and returns the machine and date. Step 2: the program checks the calendar for that machine and date. Step 3: the model writes a confirmation message. The model never chooses which step comes next. Which description fits?

options.text: A workflow, because the program's code owns the order of the steps
An agent, because a model is called inside the sequence of steps
An agent, because the sequence of steps includes a calendar tool
A workflow, because the model is called fewer than four times

items.stem: Assume every model call costs $0.01. A fixed workflow always makes exactly 3 model calls per request. An agent doing the same task averages 8 model calls per request. For 500 requests, how many dollars more does the agent cost than the workflow?
The team wants one part of the makerspace assistant built as a fixed workflow. Which part is the best candidate?

options.text: Diagnosing a jammed laser cutter using whichever manual pages turn out to matter
Answering vague questions such as what a student could make with a 3D printer
Handling unusual requests that mix machine training, safety rules and scheduling
Booking a slot: check training status, check the calendar, then write the booking

items.stem: A fixed workflow is usually cheaper and more predictable than an agent. In one or two words, what does it give up?
The booking feature is a fixed workflow and works well. Which new fact would be the best reason to replace it with an agent?

options.text: Teammates say that building an agent would be more interesting work
Requests now need steps that cannot be listed in advance for each case
The workflow costs slightly less per request than an agent would cost
Every booking request has needed the same checks in the same order
